items.title: 68003_Eddie Sauter oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee (Eddie Sauter) does not mention Wolpe. The mention of Wolpe is made by the Interviewer, who describes him as a teacher and inspiration, and notes Charlie Parker sought lessons. Sauter's previous turn discusses Schoenberg and Bartok/Stravinsky, showing no personal connection to Wolpe.

ctx.x: this work. What Bartok and Stravinsky were doing in those days was not I might have been used to hearing. How that fit into the total thing fascinated me and I did want to learn about it. I wanted to learn about [Schoenberg] Shurenberg (phonetic spelling); I never got quite to Shurenberg. It never turned me on the way the other did; it still doesn't.
Wolpe was a twelve tone writer, but what a good teacher, what an inspiration- al human being he was.
Apparently Charlie Parker had gone to him and asked for lessons.
